 When will NC election results be certified? Here's what happens after Election Day 
 Before county results are finalized, election officials must determine whether provisional ballots should be counted. Those can include ballots cast by voters who encountered issues involving registration or photo identification. By Tamara Scott Thursday, November 5, 2026 7:06PM Share RALEIGH, N.C. (WTVD) -- Election Day is over, but the process of finalizing North Carolina's results is not.
 Election officials across the state still have several steps to complete before the results become official , including reviewing provisional ballots, conducting audits and completing the canvass process. With some races still close, unofficial results could change as additional eligible ballots are added.
 All 100 county boards of elections are scheduled to complete their canvasses on Nov. 13.
 The North Carolina State Board of Elections is scheduled to certify statewide results on Nov. 24.
 Before county results are finalized, election officials must determine whether provisional ballots should be counted. Those can include ballots cast by voters who encountered issues involving registration or photo identification.
 Election officials also must process eligible absentee ballots and military and overseas ballots. Federal law provides special absentee voting protections for qualifying military members, their families and U.S. citizens living overseas.
 County election officials will also hand-count a sample of ballots as part of the post-election audit process before the Nov. 13 canvass.
 The certification process could have significant political consequences, particularly for the balance of power in the North Carolina General Assembly.
 Andrew Taylor, a political science professor at NC State, said the final makeup of the legislature remains uncertain.

 "It's unclear at the moment, although I think it looks as though the Republicans will hold on to the Senate with the slimmest majority of 26 Republicans to 24 Democrats," Taylor said.
 Taylor said the legislative dynamics could still create opportunities, and perhaps a necessity, for bipartisan cooperation.
 "Certainly there are significant opportunities. There are always opportunities to reach across the aisle. There may be necessity to reach across the aisle for Democrats, with the Republicans maintaining control of the Senate."
 The certification process may not be the final step in every contest. Candidates in qualifying close races may seek recounts before results are finalized.
